text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — noticing a ~3x uptick in Xid 13/31 across several racks since 03:00UTC. Quick eyeball shows a strong skew to small-batch decode ops. I'm starting a stratified sample; will post counts. :rotating_light:

Liam O'Neill: ugh. which region?

Maya Chen: eu-west1 and us-west2 primarily. Rough time window 02:45-03:30UTC.

Kai Park: can you paste the query you ran? I'll run a separate aggregation from metrics pipeline.

Maya Chen: sure — ran ad-hoc in telemetry: ```SELECT xid_code, op_type, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM gpu_xid_events WHERE ts >= 1719898800 AND ts <= 1719901200 GROUP BY xid_code, op_type ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 50;```

Maya Chen: sample output: ```
# xid_code | op_type       | cnt
13         | decode_small  | 423
31         | decode_small  | 198
79         | embedder      | 34
48         | decode_large  | 12
13         | sampling      | 9
```

Dennis Ortiz: decode_small dominating makes me think of syscall/timeout path or a kernel driver issue triggered by tight loops (small sequences). Any common tenant/commit?

Maya Chen: initial tenant breakdown: ~70% from two internal heavy-traffic tenants (tenant-42, tenant-77) but also spread to other tenants at low rates. doing stratified sample by tenant+op_type now.

Kai Park: i'm running a separate cohort query to correlate with driver version and fab batch: ```SELECT gpu_card, driver_version, firmware, COUNT(*) FROM gpu_xid_events WHERE xid_code IN (13,31) AND ts BETWEEN 1719898800 AND 1719901200 GROUP BY gpu_card, driver_version, firmware HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;```

ops-bot: drain requested: rack-eu-west1-12 node-045 -> initiated by Maya Chen at 1719901280

Maya Chen: thanks — I'm going to soft-drain node-045 and tag it for telemetry capture. please don't hard-replace yet; want to validate if it's workload-specific. :thumbsup:

Liam O'Neill: if we can collect the nvml logs around failures that'd be ideal — please `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,ESM` right after reproductions. Also temperature/voltage traces.

Maya Chen: pulled NVML snippet from node-045 around first failure: ```
Timestamp: 2024-05-04T03:02:11Z
Temperature GPU: 72 C
SM Utilization: 98 %
Memory Utilization: 64 %
ECC Errors (corrected): 0
PCIe Link Retrain Count: 1
Last Xid: 13
```

Dennis Ortiz: temps are high but within our 85C threshold. PCIe retrain count is interesting — could be noisy link causing decode pipeline to resend/timeout. Any NIC error counters?

Kai Park: running NIC counters now. preliminary: socket drops increased by ~0.4% for that node in window, but nothing huge. Could be packet bursts aligned with small-batch decode behavior causing queueing.

Liam O'Neill: hypothesis list: 1) driver/firmware mismatch -> causes Xid13/31 under tight decode loops 2) noisy PCIe link / PCIe switch firmware -> retrain triggers decode failure 3) workload pattern (small-batch, high-FPS) hitting a runtime bug. We should triage in that order.

Maya Chen: driver/firmware correlation query summary: ```
- node-045 (gpu-0..3): driver 525.85, firmware 91.3 -> 312 Xid13/31 combined
- node-109 (gpu-0..1): driver 525.85, firmware 90.7 -> 9 events
- node-198: driver 528.11, firmware 92.1 -> 1 event
```

Maya Chen: looks like driver 525.85 + firmware ~91.x on eu-west1 racks is overrepresented.

Dennis Ortiz: ok that suggests a driver/firmware interaction. Do we have a rolling change that landed recently? CI/auto-image?

Kai Park: image promo last night updated runtime library to 525.85 in eu-west1 group. We can pin a candidate rollback to 525.73 and run A/B on a small fleet.

Liam O'Neill: propose plan: 1) isolate 3 suspect nodes, collect full NVML+syslogs for 24h 2) temporarily route small-batch decode traffic away from suspect nodes (policy) 3) rollout driver rollback on 5 nodes as test 4) if reduces Xid rate -> schedule fleet rollback and vendor ticket.

Maya Chen: implementing step 2 now — adding policy to scheduler to prefer other racks for op_type=decode_small for next 2h. will monitor.

ops-bot: scheduler-rule-update: prefer-not-rack=euw1-hot for op_type=decode_small applied at 1719901322 by Maya Chen

Liam O'Neill: for sampling we should capture: pre/post-driver counts, per-gpu Xid rate per minute, pci retrain counts, nvlink error counters, pcie throughput stalls, and tenant session traces. I'll open a kanban card.

Maya Chen: opened INF-6789 with checklist and attached query snapshots. Adding Dennis for firmware rollback runbook.

Dennis Ortiz: noted. I'll prepare rollback playbook and vendor contact info. If vendor asks for reproducer, we'll need a short replay harness — small-batch decode loop at 40 QPS with the same model and token sizes.

Kai Park: i can spin up replay harness in staging with driver 525.85 and 525.73 to compare. timeline ~1h.

Maya Chen: thanks. if replay reproduces locally we can avoid broad rollback and instead schedule targeted driver patch.

Liam O'Neill: also add metric to alert engine: rate(Xid13|Xid31) per rack > 20/min -> automated soft-drain and page oncall. Current threshold had been per-node; catching at rack-level is helpful.

Maya Chen: agreed. adding alert now.

ops-bot: soft-drain completed on node-045 at 1719901345; traffic shifted to node-046.

Maya Chen: quick interim observation: after scheduler pref, Xid13/31 counts on rack-eu-west1 dropped 78% in the first 10 minutes. Still collecting full telemetry but promising. :thinking:

Dennis Ortiz: good signal. keep collecting PCIe retrain deltas and driver logs. If rollback test confirms, escalate to vendor with cohort-correlated logs (driver version, firmware, op_type distribution).

Kai Park: replay harness up in staging. running A/B now (525.85 vs 525.73) with 2000 small-batch requests. Will post results.

Maya Chen: thanks team. i'll update INF-6789 with telemetry dumps and next steps.

Liam O'Neill: thumbs if we should proceed with rollback if A/B shows >50% reduction. :thumbsup: :thumbsdown:

Maya Chen: +1

Dennis Ortiz: +1

ops-bot: thread closed for updates on INF-6789 at 1719901360
